subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan - FastRetail
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan - FastRetail

Hi Ella —

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for sharing details about FastRetail's priorities. Below is a concise recap from our call and a proposed PoC/onboarding plan so we can align on next steps. Please tell me if I've missed anything.

Quick recap (pain points):
- Latency spikes during flash sales: 95th percentile tail latency often breaches 600–800ms for personalization+recommendation calls.
- Cost at scale: per-request inference cost and excessive instance idle time during off-peak periods.
- Data residency & security: certain user event data must remain in your VPC for EU customers (future requirement), and you need KMS-backed key management.

Current stack you shared:
- Frontend caches + Node.js service layer calling an in-house model host (Triton) behind AWS ALB; occasional fallback to SageMaker for large-batch exports.
- Model: in-house transformer-based ranking model (~2B params).
- SLOs: 95th pctl latency target <= 200ms for interactive flows; throughput target ~120 qps during campaign peaks.

Success criteria for the PoC:
- Demonstrate 95th pctl latency <= 200ms at target throughput with cost <= current baseline by 15% or better.
- End-to-end integration with your Node.js service, minimal code changes (SDK + REST).
- Confirm VPC/private deployment options satisfy data residency needs.

Proposed PoC & onboarding plan (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, sign SOW (attached stub), and schedule technical kickoff.
- Week 1: Integration — install Redwood SDK (Python + Node.js supported), verify API compatibility, initial traffic routing (shadow mode).
- Week 2: Tuning & quantization testing — try 8-bit quantization profile, kernel selection tuning for latency.
- Week 3: Load test & reliability — controlled ramp to 120 qps, monitor 95th pctl + cost.
- Week 4: Evaluation & next steps — shared metrics, decision on Dedicated vs Private deployment, procurement path.

Owners & next meeting:
- Ben Carter (me): commercial lead + schedule coordination.
- Marissa Cole: onboarding and PoC project manager.
- Aditya Rao (solutions engineer): technical kickoff, integration deep-dive.

Requested next meeting: technical kickoff with Aditya and your platform team — propose Nov 6 or Nov 9 (US PST).

Attachments:
- FastRetail_PoC_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW stub)

Questions I had for you (please confirm):
1) Will you be able to provide a staging dataset or replay traffic for realistic load tests?
2) Any procurement timeline constraints (target vendor sign-off date)?
3) Which SDK do you prefer first: Node.js (server-side) or Python (batch/ops)?

Thanks — happy to iterate on the plan.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0184

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan - FastRetail

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap and timeline; this looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side:

- Success criteria: can we make the cost target a delta (e.g., 15% reduction over baseline) but also include an acceptable upper bound for infra spend during load tests? We need predictable budgets for the procurement review.
- Data residency: EU data must remain in our EU VPC. Would Redwood Private be required for that, or can Dedicated in eu-west-1 with customer-managed VPC peering work?
- Security: please send the SOC 2 + KMS detail or a short summary for our security team to review. I'll attach our standard security questionnaire (separate doc).
- SDK preference: Node.js first — that's where our latency-sensitive calls originate. We'll use Python for offline batch tuning if needed.

Procurement: procurement has a tentative vendor decision meeting on Nov 20, so we'd like the PoC to complete and the estimation to be available before then.

We can do Nov 6 at 10:00 AM PST for the technical kickoff. Please loop in Aditya.

Thanks,
Ella
Platform Engineering Manager
FastRetail Inc.
ella@fastretail.com
+1 (206) 555-8822

Hi Ella —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few notes responding to your points: 

- Cost target: happy to commit to delivering a PoC report that includes a cost delta versus your baseline and an expected upper-bound for projected infra spend during the load test. We'll include conservative estimates for burst.
- Data residency: both options are possible. For strict in-VPC control for EU data, Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane with on-prem or VPC options) is the safest route. However, we can also do Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 with customer-managed VPC peering and strict routing policies if that meets your security team's requirements. We'll surface both options in the final proposal.
- Security & KMS: attaching a short SOC 2 summary + KMS integration note for your security team to review. In short: we support KMS/HSM integrations and can run in a customer VPC for Private deployments; logs/audit trails available per our compliance package.
- SDK: we'll prioritize Node.js. Aditya will bring an integration checklist to the kickoff to minimize friction (runtime requirements, auth snippets, and example calls).

I've attached the SOW stub (same as earlier) and a one-page SOC2 + KMS note. 

Next steps:
- Technical kickoff: Nov 6, 10:00 AM PST — Aditya (solutions engineer) will run the session and request your staging endpoints + sample traffic if available.
- I'll have Marissa draft a PoC timeline and resource commitments after the kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Ben
